correctness.rationale: Every finite poset has a maximal point; its strict predecessor ideal determines the extension. Exact degree-preserving permutation canonicalization is a complete isomorphism test and produces the published 16999 eight-element classes. Global shared-palette directed color refinement stabilizes at 113375 colors after seven refinement steps and has exactly 16997 distinct graph-histogram classes: two doubletons and no other coincidences. Both pairs are shown directly C2-equivalent by their (4,4) and (2,4,2) equitable partitions and nonisomorphic via connectivity or cover-edge count. Isolated-point extension proves all-order existence. Full standard-library script independently rerun from embedded path, with exact witness and transitivity assertions.

value.rationale: This is the first natural size cutoff for the failure of unrestricted C2 recognition of finite posets, and the complete two-pair first layer identifies separate sources of lost mathematical structure: connectivity and Hasse covering-edge count. Both are standard poset properties, not arbitrary parameters. The exact cutoff and first-layer census are nontrivial to determine from generic theorems and can guide finite-model-theoretic experiments and comparisons with stronger variable logics. The finite claim is self-contained and remains meaningful without a general all-order class-count theorem.
